doc.title: Ruth Brisbane interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

title: Music in the Brooklyn home and her parents
summary: Her mother played piano by ear, came from a musical family; her father was a mechanic and longshoreman with no ear for music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I see. And when your mom listened to records, were they LPs?

Well LPs hadn’t even come out then. The house was always loaded with music because I have older brothers and sisters, and my mother wanted to know where they were so they were allowed to have company so there was always music and people, young people. So whatever was the latest tunes were being played around the house. But my mother could play piano, whatever she heard.
Oh, she was a person who could just hear it and then —

Yes, right. She had an ear. Her father played cornet in, I guess, minstrel bands. Yes. But her mother was a singer also, and I don’t know, on the road. My mother was raised by some aunts. But the music was in her, and I guess it came from the womb. And she imparted it to us. My father had no rhythm and couldn’t hold a tune.
How interesting. Was he mystified by your interest in music and thinking of it as a career? How did he feel about that?
Well he didn’t — he died so he really didn’t get to see me fulfill my career. And he was so busy working.
He was a mechanic. During the war, a longshoreman.
And you grew up in Brooklyn.
I grew up in Brooklyn, yes.
